foot.note: Per marching day. Engels table 7 / ch.1: Macedonian army averaged ~15 mi (24 km)/day, fastest whole-army average 19.5 mi (31 km)/day. Van Creveld: 15 mi/day steady "since time immemorial", 18th-c. armies seldom >10 mi (16 km)/day for long. FM 101-10 (1941) march table: 12-15 mi/day for a division, 15-20 for smaller units. Dupuy (dupuyinstitute.org verities): opposed advance ~17 km/day Napoleonic, ~26 km/day 1973.

horse.note: FM 101-10 (1941) par. 38 march table: cavalry (animal elements) 35 mi (56 km)/day normal march, "under conditions requiring maneuver, these rates may be increased". Low 25 mi/day for mixed horse columns; high ~50 mi (80 km)/day forced cavalry marches (educated guess for steppe horse armies with remounts).

wagon.note: FM 101-10 (1941): horse-drawn artillery / pack 20 mi (32 km)/day. Low: Engels, ox carts 2 mph for 5 h/day = 10 mi (16 km). High: van Creveld, horse-drawn transport in 1914 "twenty-five miles per day being reckoned as a steady average" (40 km).

rail.note: FM 101-10 (1941) par. 40: military trains average 20 mph (480 km per 24 h continuous), allow 3 h to load and 3 h to unload. Low: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2nd_SS_Panzer_Division_Das_Reich, unopposed rail move of ~700 km "would have taken three or four days" (175-233 km/day for a whole division incl. loading).

motorized.note: Van Creveld (WWII ch.): truck companies at "the regulation 100 miles per day" (160 km). Low: 1967 campaign, no army "stands much chance of covering more than forty miles per day" (64 km). High: FM 101-10 (1941) march table, trucks/motorized units 175 mi (280 km)/day normal march.

mechanized.note: Van Creveld conclusion: tracked vehicles can do 15 mph but no army sustained 75 mi (120 km)/day "for more than a very few days". High: FM 101-10 (1941) light & medium tanks 150 mi (240 km)/day road march. Mid 100 km = sustained operational pace between these; low 40 km = 1967 ceiling (64) minus friction.

tracked_heavy.note: FM 101-10 (1941): tractor-drawn heavy artillery 40 mi (64 km)/day; tanks 150 mi/day road march. Heavy tracked formations are limited by track wear and fuel (Das Reich 1944 road march: "steel tracks of the tanks ... wore out", https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2nd_SS_Panzer_Division_Das_Reich). Mid 70 km composite, grade C.

air.note: Operational redeployment of an air unit per day incl. ground echelon. Spitfire ferry range 1,800 km, B-17 cruise 293 km/h, F-16 cruise 933 km/h (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supermarine_Spitfire, Boeing_B-17_Flying_Fortress, General_Dynamics_F-16_Fighting_Falcon). Mid = one ferry leg of ~1,000 km per day with support; grade C.

sea.note: Envelope of naval.speedKmDay: sail 90-270 km/day (Casson), oared 90 km/day (trireme 6 kn), steam 450 (Liberty ship 11 kn), modern up to ~900 (20 kn). Mid 250 km/day for a mixed pre-modern/modern lift.

water.note: Impassable to land formations (ENGINE.md section 5: water cells need sea lift). Placeholder 0.

plains.note: Off-road multiplier. FM 101-10 (1941) march table cross-country vs road (day): foot 1.5/2.5 mph = 0.6; cavalry 5/6 = 0.83; trucks 8/25 = 0.32; tanks 15/25 = 0.6.

cropland.note: Off-road multiplier (derived:qjm-terrain-proxy) = plains FM 101-10 (1941) off-road ratio (low 0.32 trucks, mid 0.6 foot, high 0.83 cavalry) x QJM terrain mobility factor rm / rm(flat bare hard 1.05). rm from Dupuy NPW 1985 Table 1 as reproduced in Clark 1989, https://archive.org/details/dimensionalnalys1094526997, Fig. 42 p.63 (fetched, page image read): rugged heavily wooded 0.4, rugged mixed 0.5, rugged bare 0.6, rolling heavily wooded 0.6, rolling mixed 0.8, rolling bare 1.0, flat heavily wooded 0.7, flat mixed 0.9, flat bare hard 1.05, flat desert 0.95, "rolling dunes" 0.3, swamp-jungle 0.3, swamp mixed or open 0.4, urban 0.7. rm is the QJM effect of terrain on the mobility of an attacking force, so using it as a march-rate ratio is a proxy (grade C); check: the same arithmetic gives hills (rolling mixed) 0.6 x 0.8/1.05 = 0.46 and mountains (rugged mixed) 0.29 against the independent FM 101-10 climb-based 0.5 and 0.3. Cropland: flat mixed 0.9/1.05 = 0.857 -> mid 0.6 x 0.857 = 0.51, low 0.32 x 0.857 = 0.27, high 0.83 x 0.857 = 0.71. Was 0.32/0.6/0.83 C (plains copied).

Forest: flat heavily wooded 0.7/1.05 = 0.667, rolling heavily wooded 0.6/1.05 = 0.571, mean 0.619 -> mid 0.6 x 0.619 = 0.37; low 0.32 x 0.571 = 0.18; high 0.83 x 0.667 = 0.55. Was 0.2/0.4/0.6 D.

hills.note: FM 101-10 (1941) note: add 1 hour per 1,000 ft of climb. An 8 h march with ~1,500-3,000 ft of climb = 8/9.5-8/11 = 0.73-0.84 of road speed, times the 0.6 off-road ratio = ~0.45-0.5. Cross-check: QJM rolling mixed rm 0.8/1.05 x 0.6 = 0.46 (Clark 1989, https://archive.org/details/dimensionalnalys1094526997).

mountains.note: FM 101-10 (1941): +1 h per 1,000 ft climb; 4,000-8,000 ft of climb per 8 h march gives 8/12-8/16 = 0.5-0.67 on tracks, times off-road 0.6 = 0.3-0.4; vehicles lower. Cross-check: QJM rugged mixed rm 0.5/1.05 x 0.6 = 0.29 (Clark 1989, https://archive.org/details/dimensionalnalys1094526997).

Desert: flat desert 0.95/1.05 = 0.905 -> mid 0.6 x 0.905 = 0.54, high 0.83 x 0.905 = 0.75; dunes 0.3/1.05 = 0.286 -> low 0.32 x 0.286 = 0.09 (trucks in sand sea). FM 90-3 (1993, https://archive.org/details/MManuals, fetched text) gives no numeric speeds, only that desert speed "varies depending on surface texture" and that wheeled vehicles have a lower average speed in poor terrain. Water limits are in logistics. Was 0.25/0.5/0.8 D.

steppe.note: Open firm grassland: between FM 101-10 (1941) foot (0.6) and cavalry (0.83) cross-country ratios; mid 0.7.

Was 0.5/0.7/0.9 D (street-network guess).

ice.note: FM 101-10 (1941) par. 38b: snow >= 24 in prohibits marching without skis/snowshoes; trained troops on snowshoes 1.5-2.25 mph, skis 1.5-3.5 mph vs 2.5 mph road. Ice sheets/tundra assumed deep snow most of the year.

roadBonus.note: Road / cross-country speed from FM 101-10 (1941) march table: foot 2.5/1.5 = 1.67, cavalry 6/5 = 1.2, trucks 25/8 = 3.1. Applied on road cells so that terrain x roadBonus ~ 1 on plains for foot.

spring.note: Educated guess: thaw and spring rains (rasputitsa) on unpaved roads. Weather odds (movement.weatherOdds) source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin climate table, Dahlem 1961-1990 precipitation days >=1 mm (MAM 27, JJA 28, SON 27, DJF 30 days) and Brandenburg 1991-2020 snow-cover days >=1 cm (MAM 2.8, SON 1.4, DJF 20.1). rain = precip days / season days; snow = snow-cover days / season days; mud share is an educated guess (days after rain/thaw with saturated unpaved ground); clear = remainder.

summer.note: Reference season: campaign rates (Engels, van Creveld, FM 101-10) are mostly summer rates. Van Creveld: campaigns "normally started" in April. Weather odds (movement.weatherOdds) source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin climate table, Dahlem 1961-1990 precipitation days >=1 mm (MAM 27, JJA 28, SON 27, DJF 30 days) and Brandenburg 1991-2020 snow-cover days >=1 cm (MAM 2.8, SON 1.4, DJF 20.1). rain = precip days / season days; snow = snow-cover days / season days; mud share is an educated guess (days after rain/thaw with saturated unpaved ground); clear = remainder.

autumn.note: Educated guess: shortening days and autumn rains; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Barbarossa: Oct 1941 rain "turned the unpaved road network into mud, and slowed the German advance". Weather odds (movement.weatherOdds) source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin climate table, Dahlem 1961-1990 precipitation days >=1 mm (MAM 27, JJA 28, SON 27, DJF 30 days) and Brandenburg 1991-2020 snow-cover days >=1 cm (MAM 2.8, SON 1.4, DJF 20.1). rain = precip days / season days; snow = snow-cover days / season days; mud share is an educated guess (days after rain/thaw with saturated unpaved ground); clear = remainder.

winter.note: Educated guess: ~8 h daylight vs ~16 h in summer at 52N limits marching hours; frozen ground can help vehicles. Snow itself is in weather. Weather odds (movement.weatherOdds) source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin climate table, Dahlem 1961-1990 precipitation days >=1 mm (MAM 27, JJA 28, SON 27, DJF 30 days) and Brandenburg 1991-2020 snow-cover days >=1 cm (MAM 2.8, SON 1.4, DJF 20.1). rain = precip days / season days; snow = snow-cover days / season days; mud share is an educated guess (days after rain/thaw with saturated unpaved ground); clear = remainder.

rain.note: QJM weather effect on mobility hm, ORALFORE (1972) App. E Table 3 p. App-E10 (fetched, page image read), identical in the 1985 version reproduced by Clark 1989 (https://archive.org/details/dimensionalnalys1094526997, Fig. 42): dry-sunshine-temperate 1.0; wet-light 0.9 (extreme heat), 0.8 (temperate), 0.8 (extreme cold); wet-heavy 0.5, 0.6, 0.5. A rain day (>= 1 mm) is mostly light rain: mid 0.8, high 0.9, low 0.5 (heavy rain). Combat-mobility factor used as a march-rate ratio, so grade C. Was 0.7/0.85/0.95 D.

mud.note: Oct-Nov 1941: rain and snow "creating a glutinous mud that German tanks had difficulty traversing"; Army Group Centre offensive stalled. Magnitude (0.4) is a composite guess, grade C.

snow.note: FM 101-10 (1941) par. 38b: snow decreases foot mobility, >= 24 in prohibits marching without skis/snowshoes; trained troops on snowshoes 1.5-2.25 mph vs 2.5 mph normal (0.6-0.9); motor vehicles need chains above 6 in, snow plow above 18 in.

restDayFraction.note: Engels ch.2 n.66: army marched 15 mi/day "and halted for one day in seven" (1/7 = 0.143). Low 0.1 for forced campaigns, high 0.25 for heavy trains.
